conclusion: The retained measurements establish material repeated live Host verification cost; they do not isolate its I/O/parsing constituents or prove any new optimization. Existing allocation reductions already apply. Cross-checkpoint descriptor or authorization reuse is not a compatible shortcut. One bounded pure canonical-encoding comparison could be investigated only after its actual cost is measured.

existing_optimizations.fact: Five PathBuf limit names are already computed once per KernelBudget; parent-relative string is already retained.

Five limit reads already use fixed 129-byte stack buffers; short boot/membership reads already use borrowed 257-byte stack buffers. Long context uses the same original opened stream and heap fallback.
The previous adjacent duplicate Host call in admit_packet was already removed while retaining original history_checkpoint at every native progress boundary.
Rust1.95 File::open converts these short paths to a temporary stack C string, not a heap CString. Replacing it cannot be advertised as removing seven heap allocations.

observer_cost_boundary.work: Two monotonic stamps, two calling-thread CPU stamps and two nonblocking aggregate try-lock/update attempts per observed Host call. The action still executes once even if measurement contention occurs.
observer_cost_boundary.measurement_limit: Host CPU stamp starts after the beginning aggregation lock and ends before final aggregation lock/update; aggregate CPU does not measure all observer overhead. Observer overhead still remains inside the enclosing real paid operation.

descriptor_reuse_rejection.decision: Do not implement a retained file/directory descriptor shortcut under the stated exact-live-observation constraint.
reasons: An open descriptor can retain a removed or replaced object and can differ from a fresh permission-checked named-path open. Current tests explicitly require renamed contents and missing-path errors to be observed on the next call.
A /proc/thread-self descriptor is bound when opened; sharing it across scoped invoking workers does not re-resolve the actual current TID.

A kept parent directory descriptor plus relative opens can continue from the old directory after the named parent changes. Comparing only the held descriptor does not preserve the original current path evidence.
Adding fresh path/permission/namespace checks around cached descriptors would require a new equivalence proof and can erase the intended savings. No such proof or measurement has been produced here.

bounded_parse_candidate.scope: Pure comparison against a canonical encoding derived from private already-validated initial Limits; not a saved Host authorization result or retained live file descriptor.
mechanism: At successful KernelBudget construction, derive the five canonical complete text encodings from the same initial validated Limits and fixed zero burst/swap. Bind them to this private immutable instance and compiled parser/profile version.
Every check retains all original fresh boot, parent identity/ownership, current-thread membership and five limit opens/complete EOF/UTF8 reads, in the original order.

Only after all five complete current texts are available, compare full raw bytes against the precomputed canonical encoding. If all match, the parsed mathematical values are the same valid initial Limits.

Any byte difference, alternative whitespace, noncanonical form or malformed value follows the original validate_limits path. Preserve the final observed-vs-original Limits comparison and original errors.
Do not use prefix-only, trimmed-only, truncated, hash-only or last-success matching. Do not cache generation/authorization/CPU/deadline decisions.
bounded_parse_candidate.why_equivalent_if_implemented_as_stated: Full equality to an encoding constructed from the same validated scalar inputs proves only those parsed values. Current path/membership/limit evidence still has to be freshly obtained on every invocation.
constraints: The actual current aggregate provides no parse-only CPU duration, so benefit is unproven and could be negligible.
Do not add this merely to obtain another green component benchmark. The original fixed-Host business/control runs remain necessary for any performance claim.
Keep all Unicode/ASCII whitespace grammar, late I/O-before-parse errors, size/UTF8/EOF and changing-values controls on the fallback.

other_low_value_candidate.description: Immutable precomputed CStr paths with fresh opens could remove short temporary path copy/NUL scanning, but not current syscalls or heap allocations.
constraints: Do not change O_CLOEXEC/large-file behavior, EINTR retry, open error mapping, actual path spelling, or per-call descriptor close.
Existing Rust1.95 short-path stack conversion makes the likely target small; no benefit is evidenced.
